 Featured York University Libraries E-Books in Omni
 AI Needs You: How We Can Change AI's Future and Save Our Own
 by
 Verity Harding
 Call Number: Online Resource
 ISBN: 9780691244907
 Publication Date: 2024
 AI Needs You argues that it is critical for society to take the lead in ensuring that AI fulfills its promise. Verity Harding draws inspiring lessons from the histories of three twentieth-century tech revolutions--the space race, in vitro fertilization, and the internet--to empower each of us to join the conversation about AI and its possible futures. Sharing her perspective as a leading insider in technology and politics, she rejects the dominant narrative, which often likens AI's advent to that of the atomic bomb. History points the way to an achievable future in which democratically determined values guide AI to be peaceful in its intent; to embrace limitations; to serve purpose, not profit; and to be firmly rooted in societal trust.
 Algorithms for the People
 by
 Josh Simons
 Call Number: Online resource
 ISBN: 9780691244006
 Publication Date: 2023
 This book looks at putting democracy at the heart of AI governance, by showing the linkages between the regulation of technology and democratic reform.
 Mastering AI: A Survival Guide to Our Superpowered Future
 by
 Jeremy Kahn
 Call Number: Online resource
 ISBN: 9781668053324
 Publication Date: 2024
 This book addresses the positive ways in which AI will reshape many aspects of our work and lives, while also exploring the risks it poses.
 Atlas of AI: Power, Politics and the Planetary Costs of Artificial Intelligence
 by
 Kate Crawford
 Call Number: Online resource.
 ISBN: 0300209576
 Publication Date: 2021
 Drawing on more than a decade of research, award-winning science, and technology writer, Crawford, reveals how AI is a technology of extraction: from the energy and minerals needed to build and sustain its infrastructure, to the exploited workers behind "automated" services, to the data AI collects from us. Rather than taking a narrow focus on code and algorithms, Crawford offers us a political and a material perspective on what it takes to make artificial intelligence and where it goes wrong. While technical systems present a veneer of objectivity, they are always systems of power. This is an urgent account of what is at stake as technology companies use artificial intelligence to reshape the world.
 The Age of AI
 by
 Henry A. Kissinger; Eric Schmidt; Daniel Huttenlocher
 Call Number: Online Resource
 ISBN: 9780316273800
 Publication Date: 2021
 Three of the world's most accomplished and deep thinkers come together to explore Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the way it is transforming human society--and what this technology means for us all. Generative AI is filling the internet with false information. Artists, writers, and many other professionals are in fear of their jobs. AI is discovering new medicines, running military drones, and transforming the world around us--yet we do not understand the decisions it makes, and we don't know how to control them.
 The AI Mirror: How to Reclaim Our Humanity in an Age of Machine Thinking
 by
 Shannon Vallor
 Call Number: Online Resource
 ISBN: 0197759076
 Publication Date: 2024
 In this book Shannon Vallor makes a wide-ranging, prophetic, and philosophical case for what AI could be, and what we can be with it. She calls us to reclaim our human potential for moral and intellectual growth, rather than losing sight of our shared humanity as we gaze dully into our AI mirrors.
 AI and Society
 by
 Christo El Morr
 Call Number: Online resource
 ISBN: 1003261248
 Publication Date: 2022
 This book addresses the impact of AI on different aspects of society. It also explores the ways in which this impact can be addressed and the directions research agendas should take to support this.
 Relationships 5.0 : how AI, VR, and robots will reshape our emotional lives
 by
 Elyakim Kislev
 Call Number: Online Resource
 ISBN: 0197588263
 Publication Date: 2022
 Relationships 5.0 reveals the ongoing epochal change in human relationships towards technology meant to fulfill emotional, intellectual, and physical needs that have until now been met by other humans.
 Who wrote this? : how AI and the lure of efficiency threaten human writing
 by
 Naomi S. Baron
 Call Number: Online Resource
 ISBN: 1503637905
 Publication Date: 2023
 To understand how AI is redefining what it means to write and think, linguist and educator Naomi Baron leads us on a journey connecting the dots between human literacy and today's technology. From nineteenth century lessons in composition, to mathematician Alan Turing's work creating a machine for deciphering war-time messages, to contemporary engines like ChatGPT, Baron gives readers a spirited overview of the emergence of both literacy and AI, and a glimpse of their possible future. Baron shows us how to work with AI and how to spot where it risks diminishing the valuable cognitive and social benefits of being literate
 The Digital Factory: The Human Labor of Automation
 by
 Moritz Altenried
 Call Number: Online Resource
 ISBN: 0226815501
 Publication Date: 2022
 'The Digital Factory' reveals the hidden human labour that supports today's digital capitalism. The workers of today's digital factory include those in Amazon warehouses, delivery drivers, Chinese gaming workers, Filipino content moderators, and rural American search engine optimizers. Repetitive yet stressful, boring yet often emotionally demanding, these jobs require little formal qualification, but can demand a large degree of skills and knowledge. This work is often hidden behind the supposed magic of algorithms and thought to be automated, but it is in fact highly dependent on human labour.
 Artificial whiteness : politics and ideology in artificial intelligence
 by
 Yarden Katz
 Call Number: Online resource
 ISBN: 023155107X
 Publication Date: 2020
 Drawing on intimate familiarity with the field and its practices, Katz asks us to see how AI reinforces models of knowledge that assume white male superiority and an imperialist worldview. Only by seeing the connection between artificial intelligence and whiteness can we prioritize alternatives to the conception of AI as an all-encompassing technological force.
 Algorithms of Oppression: How Search Engines Reinforce Racism
 by
 Safiya Umoja Noble
 Call Number: Online resource.
 ISBN: 1479833649
 Publication Date: 2018
 Algorithms of Oppression challenges the idea that search engines like Google offer an equal playing field for all forms of ideas, identities, and activities. Through an analysis of textual and media searches as well as extensive research on paid online advertising, Noble exposes a culture of racism and sexism in the way discoverability is created online.

This book answers this question by  drawing on a range of critical approaches from the social sciences and humanities,  including posthumanism, ethics and human values, surveillance studies, Black  feminism, and other strategies for social and political resistance. The authors  analyse timely topics, including bias and language processing, responsibility  and machine learning, COVID-19 and AI in health technologies, bio-AI and  nanotechnology, digital ethics, AI and the gig economy, representations of AI in  literature and culture, and many more.

 The Oxford Handbook of Ethics of AI
 by
 Markus D. Dubber (Editor); Frank Pasquale (Editor); Sunit Das (Editor)
 Call Number: Online resource
 ISBN: 9780190067397
 Publication Date: 2020
 The term "A.I." is used to refer to a broad range of phenomena, from machine learning and data mining to artificial general intelligence. The recent advent of more sophisticated AI systems, which function with partial or full autonomy and are capable of tasks which require learning and 'intelligence', presents difficult ethical questions, and has drawn concerns from many quarters about individual and societal welfare, democratic decision-making, moral agency, and the prevention of harm. This work ranges from explorations of normative constraints on specific applications of machine learning algorithms today - in everyday medical practice, for instance - to reflections on the (potential) status of AI as a form of consciousness with attendant rights and duties and, more generally still, on the conceptual terms and frameworks necessarily to understand tasks requiring intelligence, whether "human" or "A.I."
 Unconscious Networks: Philosophy, Psychoanalysis, and Artificial Intelligence.
 by
 Luca M. Possati
 Call Number: Online Resource
 ISBN: 1003345573
 Publication Date: 2023
 This book develops an original theoretical framework for understanding human-technology relations. The author's approach, which he calls technoanalysis, analyzes artificial intelligence based on Freudian psychoanalysis, biosemiotics, and Latour's actor-network theory.
 AI Ethics
 by
 Mark Coeckelbergh
 Call Number: Online Resource
 ISBN: 9780262357067
 Publication Date: 2020
 In this book, the author, a philosopher of technology, surveys relevant philosophical discussions relating to ethics and AI including privacy concerns, responsibility and the delegation of decision making, transparency and bias, as they arise at different stages of data science processes. He also considers the future of work in an AI economy and analyzes a range of policy proposals.
 Awkward Intelligence: Where AI Goes Wrong, Why It Matters, and What We Can Do About It.
 by
 Katharina A. Zweig
 Call Number: Online Resource
 ISBN: 0262371863
 Publication Date: 2022
 This book covers areas like algorithm and machine learning in an approachable manner and engages the reader in philosophical issues relating to AI.
 Realizing the Promise and Minimizing the Perils of AI for Science and the Scientific Community
 by
 Kathleen Hall Jamieson (Editor); William Kearney (Editor); Anne-Marie Mazza (Editor)
 Call Number: Online resource
 ISBN: 1512827495
 Publication Date: 2024
 This book explores the state of AI, draws lessons from the ways in which the scientific community addresses other technologies, outlines efforts to govern AI, and recommends approaches for science to leverage AI's potential.

 by

 Call Number: Online Resource

 The integration of robotic systems and artificial intelligence into healthcare settings is accelerating. As these technological developments interact socially with children, the elderly, or the disabled, they may raise concerns besides mere physical safety; concerns that include data protection, inappropriate use of emotions, invasion of privacy, autonomy suppression, decrease in human interaction, and cognitive safety. Given the novelty of these technologies and the uncertainties surrounding the impact of care automation, it is unclear how the law should respond. This book investigates the legal and regulatory implications of the growing use of personal care robots for healthcare purposes.

 by

 Call Number: Online resource

 The Oxford Handbook of AI Governance examines how artificial intelligence (AI) interacts with and influences governance systems. It also examines how governance systems influence and interact with AI.

 Call Number: Online Resource

 Focuses on AI governance including the regulatory challenges of large-language models like ChatGPT. It treats of AI regulation, including its societal and ethical impacts and explores potential future policy directions.
 Artificial Intelligence and the Law in Canada
 by
 Ed. Florian Martin-Bariteau, Teresa Scass
 Call Number: Osgoode Stacks KF 390.5 C6 M39 2021 and Bronfman Business Library Stacks, KE 452 C6 M37 2021
 AI is poised to transform the economy, the nature of work, entire fields of human endeavor such as medicine and engineering, and the nature of government and commercial decision-making. The rapid advance of these technologies creates a need to interrogate how our existing legal frameworks can apply or how they may need to adapt to this fundamentally disruptive technology.
 Artificial Intelligence and the Law
 by
 Tshilidzi Marwala; Letlhokwa George Mpedi
 Call Number: Osgoode Stacks K 564 C6 M373 2024
 Publication Date: 2024
 A useful introductory text for legal professionals on the potential impact of AI on the law including treatment of legal and ethical concerns.
 The Cambridge Handbook of Artificial Intelligence: Global Perspectives on Law and Ethics
 by
 Larry A. DiMatteo (Editor); Cristina. Poncibò (Editor); Michel Cannarsa (Editor)
 Call Number: Online Resource
 Publication Date: 2022
 This book identifies the issues raised by AI and provides practical recommendations for regulatory, technical, and theoretical frameworks aimed at making AI compatible with existing legal rules, principles, and democratic values. An international roster of authors including professors of specialized areas of law, technologists, and practitioners bring their expertise to the interdisciplinary nature of AI.
 We, the Robots?: regulating artificial intelligence and the limits of the law
 by
 Simon Chesterman
 Call Number: Online Resource
 Publication Date: 2021
 From self-driving cars and high-speed trading to algorithmic decision-making, the way we live, work, and play is increasingly dependent on AI systems that operate with diminishing human intervention. These fast, autonomous, and opaque machines offer great benefits - and pose significant risks. This book examines how our laws are dealing with AI, as well as what additional rules and institutions are needed - including the role that AI might play in regulating itself.
 Artificial Intelligence and Intellectual Property
 by
 Reto Hilty (Editor); Jyh-An Lee (Editor); Kung-Chung Liu (Editor)
 Call Number: Online Resource
 Publication Date: 2021
 Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become omnipresent in today's business environment: from chatbots to healthcare services to various ways of creating useful information. While AI has been increasingly used to optimize various creative and innovative processes, the integration of AI into products, services, and other operational procedures raises significant concerns across virtually all areas of intellectual property (IP) law. While AI has drawn extensive attention from IP experts globally, this is the first book providing a broad and comprehensive picture from the perspectives of the very nature of AI technology, its commercial implications, its interaction with different kinds of IP, IP administration, software and data, its social and economic impact on the innovation policy, and ultimately AI's eligibility as a legal entity.

What are digital humanities?
 Digital humanities is an area of scholarly research where digital technologies and humanities disciplines meet. It can include the use of specific digital or computing tools for humanities research, or analysis of the use of such tools. More recently, researchers have begun to make use of machine learning and other AI-related technologies for work in the humanities.
For an in-depth guide on DH research, see the Digital Scholarship and Digital Humanities research guide.
In this image, Egyptian hieroglyphs are analyzed by a neural network as part of a research project at the University of Florence.

 Artificial Intelligence and Its Discontents: Critiques from the Social Sciences and Humanities
 by
 Ariane Hanemaayer (Editor)
 Call Number: Online resource
 ISBN: 9783030886141
 Publication Date: 2022
 On what basis can we challenge Artificial Intelligence (AI) - its infusion, investment,  and implementation across the globe? This book answers this question by  drawing on a range of critical approaches from the social sciences and humanities,  including posthumanism, ethics and human values, surveillance studies, Black  feminism, and other strategies for social and political resistance. The authors  analyse timely topics, including bias and language processing, responsibility  and machine learning, COVID-19 and AI in health technologies, bio-AI and  nanotechnology, digital ethics, AI and the gig economy, representations of AI in  literature and culture, and many more.

Further Reading
 A citizen's guide to artificial intelligence
 by
 John Zerilli et al
 Call Number: Online resource

 Artificial intelligence has generated a staggering amount of hype in the past several years. Topics covered include machine learning, and considers issues such as transparency, bias, liability, privacy, and regulation. The book discusses such issues as statistical definitions of fairness, legal and moral responsibility, the role of humans in machine learning decision systems, “nudging” algorithms and anonymized data, the effect of automation on the workplace, and AI as both regulatory tool and target.
